newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 13.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Thursday.
- President Mary Robinson made history yesterday when she was named UN High Commissioner for Human Rights.

- Cork is to get a further 600 new jobs. The new project is understood to have the backing of the state investment arm, IDA Ireland and will be discussed in the cabinet in coming weeks. - Mary Harney, leader of the Progressive Democrats, is likely to be be made Minister of Health in the new cabinet.

- A top sports administrator in Dublin has emerged as a key figure in a multi-million pound money laundering operation for Irish and British criminals organising a massive drug trafficking and tax evasion scam.
- Political parties must gear up for another election campaign after the announcement of President Mary Robinson's appointment as UN High Commissioner for Human Rights.
- Parents last night voiced fears that university fees could be reintroduced "by the back door" after the introduction of new levies by two colleges.
- The Irish economy is growing faster than expected, according to internal Department of Finance forecasts which forsee the number of jobs being created to be well ahead of previous forecasts.

- President Mary Robinson will meet the U.N. Secretary-General next month to discuss whether she wil cut short her presidency after her nomination as UN High Commissioner for Human Rights. - Substantial reassurance is provided for Ireland on three key areas of concern in the final draft of the Amsterdam treaty issued by the Dutch EU presidency last night. The text secures for the time being the right of each EU nation to name a Commissioner and makes substantial advance on the introduction of passport-free travel across the bloc.
